items.title: Evolving climate architecture
items.desc: PAKISTAN stands at a crossroads as it prepares to attend COP31 in Turkiye next week. Every October, the Emissions Gap Report brings bad news, and every October we read it as a scorecard of how far the world is from Paris. This year, it is not a progress report. Russian President Vladimir Putin met Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei at the Kremlin, the president's office said on Thursday.

items.title: Saudi coalition says it intercepted missile fired at Medina
items.desc: Saudi coalition says it intercepted missile fired at Medina The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis on Thursday said it intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the group at the Medina region, home to one of Islam's holiest cities. The announcement came just minutes after the kingdom's civil defence agency warned of potential danger in the area near the strategic port of Yanbu. It was unclear if the two events were connected. "Air defence intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the Medina region," coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki

items.title: Pakistan builds record reserves amid Gulf war
items.desc: KARACHI: Despite the Gulf war’s impact on weaker economies and uncertainty over high oil prices, Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves climbed to a record high of more than $26.8 billion, the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) reported on Thursday. The war started on Feb 28, jolting many economies, including Pakistan, but the SBP has since improved its reserves and added over $5bn.
